annotation_caveats.issue: The question asks which events Jon participated in; D8:4 is Gina discussing offers/promotions for her own online store. Recovering this ID is not established evidence of answering the question better. Kept in all raw annotation metrics; not silently excluded.

limitations: Coverage does not establish semantic entailment, answer correctness or source precision.
The maxEvidence=100 ablation is diagnostic only; production candidates retain 32 evidence and 6000 token budgets.
Some previously packed non-gold sources are displaced; their usefulness is unknown without paired Answer/Judge review. Each displacement is listed per question.

A time query may ask when someone mentioned a fact rather than when the underlying event occurred. Observation anchors remain useful evidence and remain in returned content. The second patch only removes a uniform fact-over-raw ranking advantage from unresolved anchors; it is not a semantic proof that observation dates are irrelevant.
Candidate collection is unchanged. Commonality/actor matching and the q0003 candidate losses remain unresolved.
This is one known conversation; lifecycle tests and source retention are necessary but not proof of generalization.
recommendation: Keep both commits as separate candidates; do not merge into the running baseline. Run paired Answer/Judge QA on all 72 questions from the same frozen snapshot before adopting either. First patch preserves raw information that has no exact fact twin. Second patch gives a temporal ranking advantage only to resolved event dates (legacy explicit time text is normalized). Neither changes candidate limits, terminal budgets, source visibility or ingestion.
